# Mexico City Family Dining Plan: Dec 20–24, 2026

A **family of 4** can stay near **3,500 MXN/day** by mixing street food, casual sit-down meals, and one nicer dinner or lunch. I’ve kept each day balanced with **at least one vegetarian choice** and **one kid-friendly meal**.

# Five-Day Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner Plan

## Day 1 — Sunday, Dec 20: Roma Norte + Condesa
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Breakfast:** Chilaquiles or huevos rancheros at a café in **Roma Norte** — **700 MXN** total
- **Lunch:** Tacos al pastor + veggie quesadillas from a casual taquería in **Condesa** — **1,000 MXN** total
- **Dinner:** Sit-down Mexican dinner in **Roma Norte** with one vegetarian main for the adults and simple rice/chicken options for kids — **1,600 MXN** total
- **Day total:** **3,300 MXN**
- **Best fit:** Easy walking neighborhoods, lots of family-friendly cafés, and plenty of backup options

## Day 2 — Monday, Dec 21: Centro Histórico + Alameda
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Breakfast:** Pan dulce and coffee/chocolate at a traditional bakery near **Centro Histórico** — **500 MXN** total
- **Lunch:** Street tacos, sopes, and a vegetarian quesadilla stop near **Alameda Central** — **1,100 MXN** total
- **Dinner:** Casual sit-down fonda or family restaurant in **Centro Histórico** with soups, enchiladas, and a kid-friendly combo plate — **1,700 MXN** total
- **Day total:** **3,300 MXN**
- **Best fit:** Good for a sightseeing day; keep lunch flexible and light

## Day 3 — Tuesday, Dec 22: Coyoacán
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Breakfast:** Café breakfast with fruit, eggs, and coffee in **Coyoacán** — **650 MXN** total
- **Lunch:** Market-style meal around **Mercado de Coyoacán**: tostadas, quesadillas, and vegetarian fillings — **1,050 MXN** total
- **Dinner:** Sit-down dinner in **Coyoacán** with grilled meats, nopales, and kid-friendly chicken or pasta — **1,500 MXN** total
- **Day total:** **3,200 MXN**
- **Best fit:** One of the easiest neighborhoods for a relaxed family meal day

## Day 4 — Wednesday, Dec 23: Polanco
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Breakfast:** Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery in **Polanco** — **700 MXN** total
- **Lunch:** Higher-quality casual lunch: tacos, bowls, or sandwiches with a vegetarian option — **1,000 MXN** total
- **Dinner:** Nicer sit-down restaurant in **Polanco** with shared plates and a children’s-friendly menu if available — **1,700 MXN** total
- **Day total:** **3,400 MXN**
- **Best fit:** Best day for a polished dinner while still staying within budget

## Day 5 — Thursday, Dec 24: San Ángel + Roma Sur
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Breakfast:** Light breakfast in **San Ángel** — pastries, fruit, and coffee — **550 MXN** total
- **Lunch:** Street-food lunch in **Roma Sur**: tacos, tortas, and vegetarian quesadillas — **1,050 MXN** total
- **Dinner:** Early family dinner at a calm sit-down restaurant in **San Ángel** or **Roma Sur** with soup, enchiladas, and simple kid plates — **1,700 MXN** total
- **Day total:** **3,300 MXN**
- **Best fit:** A calmer final day with easy dinner timing for the holiday evening

## Neighborhood Strategy for the Best Family Mix

- **Roma Norte / Condesa:** Best for cafés, easy walking, and flexible menus
- **Centro Histórico:** Best for classic Mexican food and affordable street-food lunches
- **Coyoacán:** Best for a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere and market meals
- **Polanco:** Best for one higher-end meal without blowing the budget
- **San Ángel:** Best for a quieter final-day dinner and pleasant daytime dining

## Budget Pattern That Works

- **Breakfast:** 500–700 MXN
- **Lunch:** 1,000–1,100 MXN
- **Dinner:** 1,500–1,700 MXN
- **Daily target:** **3,200–3,400 MXN**
- This leaves a small cushion for drinks, extra tortillas, desserts, or service.
